readings.title: The Weight of Divine Leadership and Righteous Subordination
readings.subtitle: It is the esteem of Elohim to hide a matter, and the esteem of sovereigns to search out a matter.
readings.text: [Proverbs 25:1] These too are proverbs of Shelomoh which the men of Ḥizqiyah sovereign of Yehuḏah copied: [2] It is the esteem of <dn>Elohim</dn> to hide <dn>את</dn> a matter, And the esteem of sovereigns to search out <dn>את</dn> a matter. [3] The heavens for height and the earth for depth, But the heart of sovereigns is unsearchable. [4] Take away <dn>את</dn> the dross from silver, And a vessel comes forth for the refiner. [5] Take away <dn>את</dn> the wrong from before the sovereign, And his throne is established in righteousness. [6] Do not exalt yourself before a sovereign, And do not stand in the place of great men; [7] For it is better for him to say to you, “Come up here,” Than that you should be put lower Before a noble whom your eyes have seen.

readings.title: Timely Words and the Structure of Relational Harmony
readings.subtitle: A word spoken at the right time is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
readings.text: [Proverbs 25:8] Do not go forth to strive in haste, For what would you do in the end, When your neighbour has put you to shame? [9] Plead <dn>את</dn> your case with your neighbour himself, And do not disclose <dn>את</dn> the secret of another; [10] Lest he who hears it put you to shame, And your evil report turn not back. [11] A word spoken at the right time Is like apples of gold in settings of silver. [12] A ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, Is a wise one’s reproof to an ear that hears. [13] Like the cold of snow in time of harvest Is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him, For he refreshes <dn>את</dn> the life of his masters. [14] He who boasts of his gifts falsely Is like clouds and wind without rain.

readings.title: Restraint and the Rejection of Relational Friction
readings.subtitle: A man bearing false witness against his neighbour is like a club and a sword and a sharp arrow.
readings.text: [Proverbs 25:15] Through patience a ruler is persuaded, And a soft tongue shatters a bone. [16] Have you found honey? Eat only as much as you need, Lest you be satisfied with it and vomit. [17] Make your foot rare in your neighbour’s house, Lest he gets enough of you and hate you. [18] A man bearing false witness against his neighbour Is like a club and a sword and a sharp arrow. [19] Trust in a treacherous man in time of distress Is like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint. [20] One who takes away a garment in cold weather, Is like vinegar on soda, And a singer of songs on an evil heart.

readings.title: Neutralizing Enemies and the Boundary of Self-Control
readings.subtitle: A man who has no control over his spirit is like a broken-down city without a wall.
readings.text: [Proverbs 25:21] If your enemy is hungry give him <dn>את</dn> bread to eat, And if he is thirsty give him <dn>את</dn> water to drink, [22] For you are heaping <dn>את</dn> coals of fire on his head, And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rewards you. [23] The north wind brings rain, And a secret tongue an enraged face. [24] It is better to dwell in a corner of a roof, Than in a house shared with a contentious woman. [25] Like cold water to a parched throat, Is good news from a distant land. [26] A righteous man who gives way before the wrong, Is like a muddied spring and a ruined fountain. [27] It is not good to eat much honey. Is it esteem to seek one’s own esteem? [28] A man who has no control over his spirit Is like a broken-down city without a wall.

readings.title: Establishing the Land Through Structural Justice
readings.subtitle: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; but when a wrong one rules, the people sigh.
readings.text: [Proverbs 29:1] One often reproved, hardening his neck, Is suddenly broken, and there is no healing. [2] When the righteous increase, the people rejoice; But when a wrong one rules, the people sigh. [3] He who loves wisdom gladdens his father, But a companion of whores destroys <dn>את</dn> wealth. [4] A sovereign establishes <dn>את</dn> a land by right-ruling, But one who receives bribes throws it down. [5] A man who flatters his neighbour Spreads a net for his own feet. [6] An evil man is ensnared by transgression, But the righteous sings and rejoices. [7] The righteous knows <dn>את</dn> the plea of the poor, The wrong does not understand such knowledge.

readings.title: Quelling Systemic Disharmony and Defending the Poor
readings.subtitle: The sovereign who rightly rules the poor with truth, his throne is established forever.
readings.text: [Proverbs 29:8] Scoffers ensnare a city, But the wise turn away wrath. [9] When a wise man disputes with a foolish man, Whether he rages or laughs, there is no peace. [10] Bloodthirsty men hate the perfect, And seek <dn>את</dn> the life of the straight. [11] A fool lets out all his breath, But the wise keeping it back calms it down. [12] If a ruler listens to lying words, All his servants become wrong. [13] The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives light to the eyes of both. [14] The sovereign who rightly rules the poor with truth, His throne is established forever.

readings.title: Discipline and the Protective Vision of Torah
readings.subtitle: Where there is no vision, the people are let loose, but blessed is he who guards the Torah.
readings.text: [Proverbs 29:15] A rod and reproof give wisdom, But a child unrestrained brings shame to his mother. [16] When the wrong become many, transgression increases; But the righteous look on their fall. [17] Discipline <dn>את</dn> your son, And he brings you rest and delight to your life. [18] Where there is no vision, the people are let loose, But blessed is he who guards <dn>את</dn> the Torah. [19] A servant is not disciplined by words; Though he understands, he does not respond. [20] Have you seen a man hasty in his words? There is more expectancy for a fool than for him. [21] He who deals tenderly With his servant from youth, Has him as a son in the end.

readings.title: Rejecting the Fear of Man for the High Ground of Trust
readings.subtitle: The fear of man brings a snare, but whoever trusts in YeHoVaH is set on high.
readings.text: [Proverbs 29:22] A man of displeasure stirs up strife, And a master of rage has many a transgression. [23] The pride of man brings him low, But the humble in spirit obtains esteem. [24] He who shares with a thief hates <dn>את</dn> his own life; He hears <dn>את</dn> an oath, but does not report. [25] The fear of man brings a snare, But whoever trusts in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is set on high. [26] Many seek the face of a ruler, But right-ruling for man comes from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [27] An unrighteous man Is an abomination to the righteous, And he who is straight in the way Is an abomination to the wrong.
